newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan legislator lands on contested isles.
newsitem.headline: Japan legislator lands on contested isles.

text.p: A Japanese legislator and three people accompanying him on Tuesday visited islands in the East China Sea which are the subject of a territorial dispute pitting Japan against China and Taiwan, the legislator's office said.

The group headed by Shingo Nishimura, a conservative member of the main opposition New Frontier Party (Shinshinto), inspected the security situation and held a brief commemorative ceremony on the Senkaku Islands, known in Chinese as the Diaoyu Islands, Nishimura's office said in a statement.
"We believe this landing on the Senkaku Islands will be the starting point for an awakening of national consciousness and the rebirth of a Japan with pride," the statement said.
Japan's coastguard, the Maritime Safety Agency, confirmed that the group landed at 8.30 a.m. (2330 GMT Monday) on the uninhabited islands, which lie 1,600 km (1,000 miles) southwest of Tokyo.
The rocky cluster of islands has ignited fiery nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan since a Japanese right wing group built a lighthouse there last July.

Nishimura and his colleagues criticised the central government in Tokyo for labelling a landing on the Senkakus last month by local assembly member from Okinawa, which administers the disputed islands, "a provocative act".
The statement said: "The Senkaku Islands are indisputably Japan's territory. It is a matter of course that a member of parliament should survey Japanese territory."
